dossier.public_summary: The 13-day dip matches the star's own rotation period and varies wildly in depth from about 200 ppm to over 1000 ppm between sectors and between individual events, while the star shows thousands of ppm spot variability. This pattern is typical of stellar activity, not a stable planet transit, so the signal is best explained by spots.

reasons.why: Depth changes by more than a factor of two between sectors (1083 to 76 ppm) with chi2=60.27 dof=5, strongly inconsistent with a single transit source.
Depth change is real within the same pipeline: SPOC 2-min p_constant=1.7854147649506313e-08 and TESS-SPOC p_constant=0.00034766755662620397, ruling out a calibration difference.
Individual transits are inconsistent (chi2=67.05 dof=10) with mean 383 ppm but outliers at 1083 ppm (sigma 5.1) and 1007 ppm (sigma 4.3) dominating the signal, share_of_top_3=0.86.

Signal period 13 d is essentially equal to the stellar rotation period 13.303 d (rotation_d 13.303) with large spot amplitudes 4519 to 13422 ppm, implying the dip is stellar variability rather than a planetary transit. xgboost.planet_rank=0.07 supports this.
Flat-bottom is misleading because the 'transits' are a sample of the star's spot modulation, not a coherent planet; RUWE=29.04 and excess_noise_sig=10230 also indicate a highly variable active star.
